138040.one: Meritz Fire ve Meritz Securities'in sahibi holding. Kalite surlarını geçti; üçüncü çeyrek kârı %26,6 düştü, fiyat testi kârın toparlanmasına bağlı.
138040.business: Meritz Financial Group bir finans holdingidir. Sigorta şirketi Meritz Fire & Marine ile aracı kurum Meritz Securities'in tamamına sahiptir; Meritz Capital da grubun içindedir. Para uzun vadeli sağlık ve koruma sigortalarından, sigorta primlerinin yatırım gelirinden ve kurumsal finansman ile gayrimenkul kredilerinden gelir. 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında konsolide net kâr 1,96 trilyon won; kârın %62'si sigortadan, %32'si aracı kurumdan, %6'sı Meritz Capital'den.
138040.moat_text: Hendek dar. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılın ortalamasında %18,6, en düşük yılında %15,8. Sigorta lisansı ve acente ağı yeni girene engel. Zayıf yanı: sigorta ve kurumsal finansman, rakiplerin de yapabildiği işlerdir; üstünlük markadan çok fiyatlama disiplinine ve yönetime dayanıyor. Şirket nakit temettü yerine bütün kaynağı geri alım ve iptale ayırıyor; hedefi konsolide net kârın %50'sini ortağa döndürmek. en.one: Holding company owning Meritz Fire and Meritz Securities. It passed the quality walls; third-quarter profit fell 26.6%, so the price test depends on profit recovering.
en.business: Meritz Financial Group is a financial holding company. It owns all of the insurer Meritz Fire & Marine and the broker Meritz Securities; Meritz Capital is also in the group. The money comes from long-term health and protection insurance, from investing the insurance premiums, and from corporate finance and real estate lending. In the first nine months of 2026 consolidated net profit was 1.96 trillion won; 62% of profit came from insurance, 32% from the securities firm and 6% from Meritz Capital.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Real return on equity averaged 18.6% over five years and was 15.8% in the weakest year. The part of the advantage that shows in numbers is the insurance book: at the end of September 2026 the contractual service margin (CSM) not yet booked as profit was 12.26 trillion won (11.10 trillion at the end of 2025), and 326.1 billion won of it moved into profit in the third quarter. The insurance licence and the agent network are a barrier to a newcomer. The weak side: insurance and corporate finance are businesses rivals can also do; the advantage rests on pricing discipline and management more than on a brand. A large part of profit depends on investment income; in the third quarter losses on shares cut the insurer's profit by 29.2%.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is Cho Jung-ho with 10 related parties: 56.13% (end of 2025). The National Pension Service holds 6.51%. Profit returns to shareholders through buybacks: between March 2023 and March 2026 the company bought back and cancelled 3.09 trillion won of shares (36 million shares, about 17.7% of those issued). In 2025 the share returned to shareholders was 61.7% of profit. The company puts all of the money into buybacks and cancellation rather than a cash dividend; its target is to return 50% of consolidated net profit. The 700 billion won programme that began in March 2026 is complete: 6,273,560 shares were bought for 703.8 billion won (an average of about 112,200 won a share; book value is 68,284 won a share). A new 500 billion won programme began on 28 August 2026; by the end of October 147.5 billion won of shares (about 1.14 million) had been bought. The company says it compares buybacks with its own 10% required return. Note: the holding company's investment in subsidiaries relative to its own equity (double leverage) rose from 112.1% in March 2026 to 127.8% in June 2026; we looked for the September 2026 ratio and it is not in the documents read. Share-based pay, goodwill and acquisitions paid in shares: checked, not in the documents read.
en.latest: 11 November 2026: Consolidated net profit in the third quarter was 490.5 billion won (668.4 billion a year earlier; −26.6%); profit attributable to the parent's owners was 470.7 billion won (654.7 billion; −28.1%). Nine-month consolidated profit was 1.96 trillion won (−3.2%) and owners' profit 1.91 trillion won (−3.9%). Earnings per share for the nine months were 11,491 won (+3.5%): buybacks reduced the share count. The reason: Meritz Fire's investment profit fell to 39.4 billion won in the quarter (325.0 billion a year earlier; −87.9%), on valuation losses on domestic shares and provisions against real estate loans. Meritz Fire's quarterly profit was 328.5 billion won (−29.2%); insurance profit, however, rose 34.9% in the quarter and 7.6% in nine months (1.10 trillion won). Meritz Securities' nine-month profit was 720.5 billion won (+12.0%) and Meritz Capital's 121.9 billion won (+23.6%). The group set aside 410.6 billion won of provisions and reserves in the quarter. The return on equity the company reports is 23.5%, return on assets 1.8%, book value per share 68,284 won, total assets 146.5 trillion won and the solvency ratio (K-ICS) 225.7% (230.5% in June). The figures are from the published copy of the exchange filing and from press reports; the company's own presentation could not be opened.
risks: The price test rests on the last 12 months' profit and on past growth; owners' profit fell 28.1% in the third quarter and nine-month profit is 3.9% below last year. If investment income does not recover, the earnings and growth in the calculation are too high.

Real estate lending is large: 29.8 trillion won in September 2026 (26.2 trillion in Korea, 3.6 trillion abroad), more than twice equity of about 12.6 trillion won. The company says 89% is senior lending and the average loan-to-value ratio is 46%. The group set aside 410.6 billion won of provisions and reserves in the third quarter (a net 187.5 billion in the second).

Credit quality is weaker than at rivals (NICE Credit Rating, June 2026): the bad-asset ratio is 6.4% at Meritz Fire (sector 1.6%), 4.2% at Meritz Securities and 9.0% at Meritz Capital; provisions cover 49.3% of bad assets at Securities and 46.5% at Capital. Loans to Homeplus were 1.17 trillion won at the end of 2025; a new 200 billion won loan was made in July 2026. Meritz Securities' off-balance-sheet commitments are 7.2 trillion won (86.3% of its equity).
Regulation affects profit directly: a higher education tax, a cap on agent commissions and rules on insurance assumptions came into force in 2026.
Control sits with one family (56.13%), and the double leverage ratio rose to 127.8% while the holding company kept buying back shares; if dividends from subsidiaries fall, the pace of buybacks slows.

They swing widely from quarter to quarter: gains of about 86 billion won in Q1 2026 and about 250 billion in Q2 2026 (pre-tax), then valuation losses in Q3; Meritz Fire's investment profit fell to 39.4 billion won in Q3 (325.0 billion a year earlier).

en.one: One of Korea's large independent insurance agencies. It passed the quality walls; the advantage rests on a sales force that must be re-recruited every year, and commission rules are changing. The moat is weak.
en.business: INCAR Financial Service is an independent agency (GA) in Korea that sells the policies of many insurers. It earns sales commissions from the insurers and pays most of them on to its own agents. In the first half of 2026 revenue was 640 billion won (+36.5%) and net profit 44.5 billion won (+34.8%). The number of agents rose from 20,651 at the end of 2025 to 24,724 at the end of June.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. The advantage comes from scale: 24,724 agents, a five-year average real return on equity of 37.4% and 29.7% in the lowest year. But this scale is won anew every year. The agents are not employees; they are recruited with settlement bonuses and can leave. Agent retention fell from 83.1% to 79.3%. In July 2026 the cap on first-year commissions (the 1200% rule) began to apply to what agencies pay their own agents; from January 2027 commissions will be spread over four years, and from 2029 over seven. The rules limit the tools an agency uses to attract agents, and the insurers' own sales forces are growing too (+11.7%). Profit is booked on an accrual basis: commissions paid in advance to agents (prepaid expenses) stand at 781.5 billion won, more than nine times annual profit; operating cash flow in the first half was minus 27.6 billion won. An advantage that has to be defended anew every year does not count as a moat in this filter.
en.mgmt: Founder and chairman Choi Byung-chae and related parties held 43.37% of the shares at the end of 2025. The company paid a dividend of 370 won a share for 2025 (2024: 100 won, 2023: 350 won). It cancelled 2,116,143 treasury shares in December 2025 and signed a 7 billion won buyback contract in June 2026. Flaws: the chairman and the president have borrowed against their shares (2,651,801 of the president's shares are pledged), and the company paid an administrative fine to the regulator after its 2024 inspection. Most of the profit stays in the company and goes into enlarging the agent force.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: In the first half revenue was 640 billion won (+36.5%), operating profit 58.3 billion won (+30.1%) and net profit 44.5 billion won (+34.8%). Second-quarter net profit was 22.0 billion won, against 22.5 billion in the first quarter. The company put the fall down to about 6 billion won of one-off costs: an administrative fine and the cost of a golf tournament. The third-quarter report had not been published on 13 November 2026.
risks: Commission rules are changing: from January 2027 sales commissions will be spread over four years, and from 2029 over seven. This changes the timing of revenue and cash; the effect on profit is not yet known.
Commissions paid in advance to agents stand at 781.5 billion won on the balance sheet. If policies lapse early or new sales slow, this asset is written off as expense.
Agents can leave: retention fell from 83.1% to 79.3%, and insurers are enlarging their own sales forces quickly.
Operating cash flow in the first half was minus 27.6 billion won; profit is not turning into cash.
The chairman and the president have borrowed against their shares; if the price falls, pledged shares could be sold.

en.one: Maker of acne patches and wound dressings. It passed the quality walls; it failed Wall 3 because more than half of sales depend on one US customer.
en.business: T&L (티앤엘) makes hydrocolloid wound dressings and acne patches, mostly for other companies' brands. In the first half of 2026 revenue was 101.1 billion won; 79.7 billion of it came from hydrocolloid products and 78.1 billion from exports. Sales to the United States were 57.4 billion won. The plants are in Yongin and Anseong.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from manufacturing know-how and scale, and it shows in the numbers: real return on equity averaged 20.4% over five years and was 15.7% in the weakest year; the operating margin in the first half of 2026 was 42.8%. The weak side is large: the brand belongs to the customer, not to the company. A single customer gave 56% of revenue in the first half of 2026 (56.7 billion won; 45% in 2025, 58% in 2024). Broker reports identify this customer as Church & Dwight, owner of the Mighty Patch brand. The same reports say that since the second quarter of 2025 the customer orders when its stock runs down instead of on a regular schedule. When the customer cut inventory in 2025, US sales fell 27% and net profit fell 18%. The company therefore did not pass criterion E (dependence on a single customer).
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is Choi Yun-so (23.70%); Choi Hyeon-jun holds 11.23%. A dividend of 1,500 won a share was paid from 2025 profit (750 won the year before), 12.0 billion won in total. Between September 2025 and September 2026 the company bought back 7.2 billion won of shares (143,491 shares); no cancellation has been announced, and the company says it may keep them for acquisitions and employee awards. A bonus issue was made in August 2026 (7,942,120 new shares; the share count became 16,070,120). There is almost no debt: cash and short-term financial assets are 104.2 billion won against total liabilities of 29.0 billion. With the related company Cosmeditech there were, in 2025, an asset sale of 5.8 billion won, outsourcing purchases of 7.8 billion and a loan of 2.0 billion.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: The company published its half-year report (a correction to the notes followed on 21 August). Second-quarter revenue was 56.0 billion won (38.8 billion a year earlier), operating profit 25.0 billion won (10.0 billion a year earlier) and net profit 19.9 billion won (7.8 billion a year earlier). First-half revenue was 101.1 billion won (+12%) and net profit 36.4 billion won (+54%). The second quarter of last year was weak because the customer was cutting inventory. The third-quarter report is due by 14 November 2026; it had not been published when this report was written.
risks: The profit of the last 12 months rests on one customer's orders: it gave 56% of first-half revenue. When the customer cut inventory in 2025 net profit fell 18%; if that happens again, profit and the calculated margin fall together.
The brand is in the customer's hands. If the customer finds a second manufacturer or takes production in-house, the filings show no contract that would prevent it.
77% of sales are exports. A stronger won or higher US tariffs would narrow the margin; first-half profit includes 3.2 billion won of currency gains.
The 44.6% operating margin of the second quarter is very high even by the company's own history; a broker estimate expects lower sales and margin in the third quarter.
There are asset sales, outsourcing purchases and loans with the related company Cosmeditech; this is something a minority shareholder should follow.

en.one: Seller of MLB and Discovery branded apparel. Passed the quality walls; failed the management test: much profit is tied up in a non-core golf fund.
en.business: F&F designs and sells clothing, caps and shoes under the MLB and Discovery Expedition brands; production is outsourced. In 2025 revenue was 1.934 trillion won and operating profit 468.5 billion won (a 24.2% margin). About half of revenue comes from China (960 billion won in 2025). The MLB brand does not belong to the company; it is used under licence. The company bought the Discovery Expedition trademark in August 2026 for 80 million dollars.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage shows in the numbers: the operating margin was 23.8% in 2024 and 24.2% in 2025; real return on equity averaged 30.5% over five years and was 20.4% in its lowest year. That margin is high for an apparel company and shows pricing power. The weak side: the largest brand, MLB, is rented, not owned; we could not find the licence term or expiry date in the documents read in this run. Earnings depend on China, and growth there has stopped: the Chinese subsidiary's revenue fell 4% in the third quarter of 2026. Real return on equity has come down from 51.8% in 2021 to the 20-25% range.
en.mgmt: The company did not pass this test (D = 0). Control lies with F&F Holdings and parties acting with it: 62.8%; the free float is 35.0%. Only a small part of profit is paid out: the 2025 dividend was 2,700 won a share, 69.3 billion won in total, against profit of 401 billion won. In 2021, 558 billion won went into the Centroid private equity fund that bought the golf equipment maker TaylorMade. The carrying amount of this stake was 718.9 billion won at the end of June 2026: 27.6% of total assets. This is a large financial investment outside the main business, and it also moves reported profit (90 billion won of equity-method income in 2025). The company is now examining a purchase of all of TaylorMade; the price being discussed is around 2.5 billion dollars, more than the company's own market value. Over five years about 85% of profit stayed in the company, while real earnings per share did not grow.
en.latest: 10 November 2026: Preliminary third-quarter results were announced. Revenue was 452.1 billion won (−4.7%), operating profit 108.4 billion won (−15.3%) and net profit attributable to owners 65.9 billion won (−32.9%). The Chinese subsidiary's revenue was 272.4 billion won (−4%): retail sales were flat and an inventory adjustment reduced shipments. The company has begun due diligence on TaylorMade; a decision is expected by the end of the year, or early 2027 at the latest. The detailed quarterly report had not been published when this was written.
risks: Profit for the last 12 months looks higher than what the main business earns: net profit attributable to owners was 492 billion won, while operating profit was 481 billion won. Most of the gap is income booked from the TaylorMade fund; if the fund is sold, or the company buys TaylorMade, that income goes away. Net profit fell 32.9% in the third quarter.
The MLB brand is rented. If the licence is not renewed, or its terms get heavier, most of the business is affected; the term and expiry date were not in the documents we read.
If TaylorMade is bought, the company will have taken on, with debt, a business larger than its own market value, and one unrelated to apparel.
About half of revenue comes from China. If demand or the exchange rate turns there, profit falls; shipments to China have been weak for two quarters in 2026.
The company is listed in Korea but earns half its revenue in China; the inflation adjustment was made with Korean inflation.

439260.business: Daehan Shipbuilding (대한조선), Güney Kore'nin Haenam kentindeki tek tersanesinde orta boy tanker yapar. Ana ürünü 157.000 tonluk Suezmax ham petrol tankeridir; parayı gemiyi yaptıkça, armatörden aldığı taksitlerle kazanır. Eylül 2026 sonunda sipariş defterinde 3,3 milyar dolarlık 35 gemi vardı: 30 Suezmax tanker, 3 mekik tanker, 2 konteyner gemisi. 2025 hasılatı 1.228,1 milyar won, faaliyet kârı 294,1 milyar won.
439260.moat_text: Hendek zayıf. Üstünlük gerçek: tersane aynı gemi tipini art arda yapıyor ve faaliyet marjı sekiz çeyrektir %20'nin üzerinde (2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde %25,3). Ama gemi siparişi teklifle alınır ve fiyatı dünya yeni gemi piyasası belirler; bugünkü marj 2024'te yüksek fiyatla alınan siparişlerin teslimine dayanıyor. Kanıt da kısa: kaynakta yalnız üç mali yılın özsermaye kârlılığı var (reel %21,1, %52,4 ve %29,2; son 12 ayda %30,6). Bir aracı kurum raporundaki rakamlara göre faaliyet marjı 2023'te %4 dolayındaydı. Döngü tersine dönünce korunacağı kanıtlanmamış bir üstünlüğü bu süzgeç hendek saymıyor; şirket B puanı 1 olduğu için 3. surda elendi.
439260.mgmt: En büyük ortak KHI: şirketi 2022'de bir ortak girişimle aldı, 2026 ortasında payı %46,7 idi. Hisse 1 Ağustos 2025'te borsaya girdi; borsa geçmişi bir yılı biraz geçiyor. Kârın küçük bölümü dağıtılıyor: Mart 2026'da 40 milyar wonluk hisse geri alınıp iptal edildi, 9,6 milyar won temettü ödendi. 10 Kasım 2026'da şirket 2027-2029 için yıllık konsolide net kârın en az %30'unu dağıtma sözü verdi ve 10 milyar wonluk yeni geri alım kararı aldı. KHI'nin eski kardeş şirketi K Shipbuilding satışta; basına göre KHI oradaki payını da satmayı planlıyor.
439260.latest: 11 Kasım 2026: Üçüncü çeyrek hasılatı 327,7 milyar won (+%19,6), faaliyet kârı 82,7 milyar won (+%24,4), net kâr 36,9 milyar won (−%43,9; geçen yıl 65,8 milyar). Basına göre net kârı kur zararı düşürdü (çeyrekte 44,7 milyar won). Dokuz ayda net kâr 193,0 milyar won (+%13,5), faaliyet kârı 260,6 milyar won (+%31,1). Rakamlar ön sonuçtur, denetimden geçmedi. Yıl içinde 1,5 milyar dolarlık 17 Suezmax siparişi alındı; yıllık hedef %62 aşıldı. 12 Kasım 2026'da 249,8 milyar wonluk iki tanker siparişi daha açıklandı (teslim Haziran 2030'a kadar).

Tek tersane, tek ana ürün: sipariş defterindeki 35 geminin 30'u Suezmax tanker.
Gelir dolarla, maliyet wonla: kur düşünce kâr düşüyor. Üçüncü çeyrekte net kâr kur zararı yüzünden %43,9 geriledi.

Geçmiş kısa: hisse Ağustos 2025'te borsaya girdi, kaynakta yalnız üç mali yılın özsermaye kârlılığı var. Hâkim ortak KHI'nin öbür tersanesi el değiştirdi; grubun para ihtiyacı küçük ortağı etkileyebilir.

en.one: A shipyard building mid-size crude oil tankers. Passed the quality walls; work is won by bidding, the high margin is recent. Eliminated at Wall 3.
en.business: Daehan Shipbuilding (대한조선) builds mid-size tankers at its single yard in Haenam, South Korea. Its main product is the 157,000-tonne Suezmax crude oil tanker; it earns its money as it builds the ship, from the instalments the shipowner pays. At the end of September 2026 the order book held 35 ships worth 3.3 billion dollars: 30 Suezmax tankers, 3 shuttle tankers and 2 container ships. Revenue in 2025 was 1,228.1 billion won and operating profit 294.1 billion won.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. The advantage is real: the yard builds the same ship type again and again, and the operating margin has been above 20% for eight quarters (25.3% in the third quarter of 2026). But ship orders are won by bidding and the price is set by the world newbuilding market; today's margin rests on deliveries of orders taken at high prices in 2024. The record is also short: the source has return on equity for only three fiscal years (21.1%, 52.4% and 29.2% in real terms; 30.6% in the last 12 months). According to the figures in a broker report, the operating margin was about 4% in 2023. This filter does not count as a moat an advantage that has not been proven through a downturn; the company was eliminated at Wall 3 because its B score is 1.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is KHI: it bought the company in 2022 with a consortium and held 46.7% in mid-2026. The shares were listed on 1 August 2025; the listed history is a little over one year. A small part of profit is paid out: in March 2026 shares worth 40 billion won were bought back and cancelled, and 9.6 billion won of dividends were paid. On 10 November 2026 the company pledged to return at least 30% of annual consolidated net profit for 2027-2029 and approved a new 10 billion won buyback. KHI's former sister company K Shipbuilding is up for sale; according to the press, KHI plans to sell its stake there as well.
en.latest: 11 November 2026: Third-quarter revenue was 327.7 billion won (+19.6%), operating profit 82.7 billion won (+24.4%) and net profit 36.9 billion won (−43.9%; 65.8 billion a year earlier). According to the press, a foreign exchange loss pulled net profit down (44.7 billion won in the quarter). Nine-month net profit was 193.0 billion won (+13.5%) and operating profit 260.6 billion won (+31.1%). The figures are preliminary and unaudited. Orders for 17 Suezmax tankers worth 1.5 billion dollars were won during the year; the annual target was exceeded by 62%. On 12 November 2026 an order for two more tankers worth 249.8 billion won was announced (delivery by June 2030).
risks: Profit depends on the cycle: today's margin comes from orders taken at high prices in 2024. If newbuilding prices or tanker demand fall, the margin on deliveries a few years out falls too.
One yard, one main product: 30 of the 35 ships in the order book are Suezmax tankers.
Revenue is in dollars and costs are in won: profit falls when the exchange rate falls. In the third quarter net profit dropped 43.9% because of a foreign exchange loss.

The record is short: the shares were listed in August 2025 and the source has return on equity for only three fiscal years. The other shipyard of the controlling shareholder KHI changed hands; the group's need for cash could affect minority shareholders.

336570.one: Cilt sıkılaştırma cihazı Oligio'nun üreticisi. Hendek ölçütünü geçemedi: reklam gideri üçe katlandı, faaliyet kârı düştü, son 12 ay kârının üçte biri nakit dışı türev kazancı.
336570.business: Wontech, cilt kliniklerine radyofrekans ve lazer cihazları satar; en bilinen ürünü cilt sıkılaştırma cihazı Oligio'dur. Para cihaz satışından ve her işlemde tüketilen uçlardan gelir. 2025'te gelir 156,8 milyar won, faaliyet kârı 51,7 milyar won oldu; gelirin %37,6'sı radyofrekans ve ultrason cihazlarından, %31,5'i lazerlerden, %24,1'i sarf uçlarından geldi. 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında gelirin %75,4'ü yurt dışından geldi; en büyük pazar Tayland.
336570.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu yüzden 3. suru geçemedi. Üstünlük var: reel özsermaye kârlılığı son beş okumada %21,4 ile %45,0 arasında, sarf uçları gelirin dörtte biri. Ama bu üstünlük 2026'da pahalıya korunuyor. Yılın ilk yarısında gelir %13,6 arttı, satış ve yönetim giderleri %79 arttı (reklam 4,3 milyar wondan 13,2 milyar wona çıktı) ve faaliyet kârı %30 düştü (31,8 milyar wondan 22,3 milyar wona). Üçüncü çeyrekte faaliyet kâr marjı yaklaşık %15 (2025 yılında %33). Ürün, Thermage gibi yerleşik markaların ve Koreli rakiplerin bulunduğu kalabalık bir alanda satılıyor; ABD ve Çin şirketleri 2025'in üçüncü çeyreğinde sermayesini yitirmiş durumdaydı ve Oligio'nun Çin onayı dört yıldır çıkmadı. Pazar payı rakamı belgelerde bulunamadı. Marka, reklam harcaması artmadan fiyatını koruyabildiğini henüz göstermedi.
336570.mgmt: Kurucu Kim ailesi yönetimde (iki eş genel müdür: Kim Jong-won ve Kim Jung-hyun); ortaklık oranları bu çalıştırmada şirket belgesinden okunamadı. Sermaye tahsisi karışık. Olumlu yan: 2026'da üç kez hisse iptali (toplam 1.891.516 hisse) ve 11 milyar wonluk geri alım sözleşmesi. Olumsuz yan: Mayıs 2026'da 75 milyar wonluk faizsiz dönüştürülebilir tahvil çıkarıldı (dönüşüm fiyatı 8.270 won, payların yaklaşık %10,1'i; fiyat 5.789 wona kadar inebilir); hisse bugün 3.530 won. Şirket aynı yıl hem pay geri alıyor hem sulandırıcı tahvil çıkarıyor. Gwacheon'da 244,5 milyar wonluk genel merkez arazisi ve binası alımı kararlaştırıldı; bu, 2025 sonu toplam varlıkların %112,5'i. Japonya'daki bir pay alımı yaklaşık dört ay geç açıklandı; borsa, özensiz açıklama işlemi başlatabileceğini bildirdi. Eylül 2026'da zarar eden Won Medico'nun %39,03'ü 13,3 milyar wona alındı. Beş yılda pay sayısı %24 arttı. Hisse bazlı ücret, şerefiye ve emeklilik yükümlülüğü: bakıldı, şirket belgesi açılamadığı için okunamadı.
336570.latest: 13 Kasım 2026: Üçüncü çeyrekte gelir yaklaşık 36,2 milyar won, faaliyet kârı yaklaşık 5,5 milyar won (marj yaklaşık %15), net zarar 2,85 milyar won. Şirket zararı kur farkından doğan nakit dışı değerleme kaybına bağladı. Dokuz aylık gelir yaklaşık 124,0 milyar won (+%12,2); yurt dışı gelir %31,6 arttı. İlk yarıda net kâr 25,9 milyar won (+%22,6) idi, ama bunun içinde dönüştürülebilir tahvile bağlı 21,2 milyar wonluk nakit dışı türev kazancı var; aynı dönemde işletme nakit akışı eksi 13,4 milyar won. Rakamlar basın haberlerinden; şirketin kendi belgesi açılamadı.
risks: Son 12 ayın kârı işin kazanç gücünü olduğundan yüksek gösteriyor: ilk yarıdaki 25,9 milyar wonluk net kârın içinde 21,2 milyar wonluk (vergi öncesi) nakit dışı türev kazancı var; üçüncü çeyrek zararla kapandı.
Reklam ve satış gideri gelirden çok daha hızlı büyüyor; ilk yarıda işletme nakit akışı eksiye döndü (alacaklar 14,2 milyar, stoklar 7,9 milyar won arttı).
244,5 milyar wonluk genel merkez taahhüdü toplam varlıklardan büyük; ödemelerin %80'i 2032'de tamamlanınca yapılacak.
75 milyar wonluk dönüştürülebilir tahvil payları yaklaşık %10 sulandırabilir; yatırımcının Mayıs 2028'den itibaren geri ödeme isteme hakkı var.
Gelirin dörtte üçü yurt dışından geliyor ve Tayland'a yoğunlaşmış; kur farkı kârı çeyrekten çeyreğe oynatıyor.

en.one: Maker of the Oligio skin-tightening device. It did not pass the moat test: advertising tripled, operating profit fell, and a third of 12-month profit is a non-cash derivative gain.
en.business: Wontech sells radio-frequency and laser devices to skin clinics; its best-known product is the Oligio skin-tightening device. The money comes from device sales and from the tips used up in each treatment. In 2025 revenue was 156.8 billion won and operating profit 51.7 billion won; 37.6% of revenue came from radio-frequency and ultrasound devices, 31.5% from lasers and 24.1% from consumable tips. In the first nine months of 2026, 75.4% of revenue came from abroad; the largest market is Thailand.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. There is an advantage: real return on equity was between 21.4% and 45.0% in the last five readings, and consumable tips are a quarter of revenue. But in 2026 that advantage is being defended at a high cost. In the first half revenue rose 13.6%, selling and administrative costs rose 79% (advertising went from 4.3 billion won to 13.2 billion won) and operating profit fell 30% (from 31.8 billion won to 22.3 billion won). The third-quarter operating margin was about 15% (33% in 2025). The product is sold in a crowded field with established brands such as Thermage and Korean rivals; the US and China subsidiaries had lost their capital as of the third quarter of 2025, and Oligio's approval in China has been pending for four years. No market share figure was found in the documents. The brand has not yet shown that it can hold its price without rising advertising spend.
en.mgmt: The founding Kim family runs the company (two co-chief executives: Kim Jong-won and Kim Jung-hyun); ownership percentages could not be read from a company document in this run. Capital allocation is mixed. On the positive side: three share cancellations in 2026 (1,891,516 shares in total) and buyback contracts of 11 billion won. On the negative side: in May 2026 the company issued a 75 billion won zero-coupon convertible bond (conversion price 8,270 won, about 10.1% of shares; the price can reset down to 5,789 won); the share trades at 3,530 won today. In the same year the company is both buying back shares and issuing a dilutive bond. It agreed to buy land and a building for a head office in Gwacheon for 244.5 billion won; that is 112.5% of total assets at the end of 2025. A stake purchase in Japan was disclosed about four months late; the exchange signalled a possible unfaithful-disclosure designation. In September 2026 it bought 39.03% of loss-making Won Medico for 13.3 billion won. The share count rose 24% in five years. Share-based pay, goodwill and pension obligations: looked for, but could not be read because the company document could not be opened.
en.latest: 13 November 2026: Third-quarter revenue was about 36.2 billion won, operating profit about 5.5 billion won (margin about 15%) and the net result a loss of 2.85 billion won. The company attributed the loss to a non-cash valuation loss from exchange rates. Nine-month revenue was about 124.0 billion won (+12.2%); overseas revenue rose 31.6%. First-half net profit was 25.9 billion won (+22.6%), but it includes a non-cash derivative gain of 21.2 billion won linked to the convertible bond; operating cash flow in the same period was minus 13.4 billion won. Figures are from press reports; the company's own document could not be opened.
risks: Profit for the last 12 months overstates the earning power of the business: first-half net profit of 25.9 billion won includes a non-cash derivative gain of 21.2 billion won (pre-tax); the third quarter closed with a loss.
Advertising and selling costs are growing much faster than revenue; operating cash flow turned negative in the first half (receivables rose 14.2 billion won, inventories 7.9 billion won).
The 244.5 billion won head office commitment is larger than total assets; 80% of the payment falls due at completion in 2032.
The 75 billion won convertible bond can dilute shares by about 10%; investors can demand repayment from May 2028.
Three quarters of revenue comes from abroad and is concentrated in Thailand; exchange differences move profit from quarter to quarter.

353810.one: Yem katkısı ve domuz yavrusu yemi üreticisi; 2024'te ABD'li Devenish'i borçla aldı. Hendek ölçütünü geçemedi: marj %10 dolayında, pazar payı kanıtı yok.
353810.business: Easy Bio, hayvan yemi katkıları ve domuz yavrusu yemi üretir. Gelirin yaklaşık %74,8'i yem katkılarından, %25,2'si karma yemden gelir. Mart 2024'te kendisinden büyük olan ABD'li Devenish Nutrition'ı satın aldı; gelir yaklaşık 165 milyar wondan 2024'te 384 milyar wona çıktı ve yurt dışı payı %60'ı geçti. 2025'te gelir yaklaşık 477 milyar won, faaliyet kârı yaklaşık 45 milyar won (marj %9,4). 2026'nın ilk yarısında gelir 278,8 milyar won, faaliyet kârı 28,3 milyar won.
353810.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu yüzden 3. suru geçemedi. Üstünlük var: özel yem katkılarında müşteri ürün değiştirmekte isteksizdir ve katkıların marjı sıradan yemin (%2-3) birkaç katıdır. Ama rakamlar dar bir hendeği kanıtlamıyor. Konsolide faaliyet kâr marjı 2022'de %10,4, 2023'te %12,5, 2024'te %8,4, 2025'te %9,4: yüksek değil ve satın almayla düştü. Pazar payı rakamı okunan hiçbir belgede yok. Karma yemde maliyetin yaklaşık %80'i tahıl; fiyat müşteriye yansıtılıyor ama bu bir emtia işidir. Yüksek özsermaye kârlılığının (son okuma reel %34,3) bir bölümü borçtan geliyor: 2024 sonunda yükümlülükler özsermayenin yaklaşık üç katıydı ve yatırılan sermayenin getirisi %14-17 aralığında kaldı. Büyüme satın almalarla geldi; Devenish'in marjı alımdan önce %4 dolayındaydı.
353810.mgmt: Ana ortak Easy Holdings ve üç ilişkili kişi: %51,53. Şirket 2020'de Easy Holdings'ten bölünerek kuruldu; grubun tavuk, ördek ve domuz çiftlikleri müşterisidir, yani ilişkili taraf satışı vardır (tutarı okunamadı). Kâr temettüye ve satın almaya gidiyor: hisse başına temettü 2022'de 75, 2023'te 100, 2024'te 200 won; dağıtım oranı %21-33. Mart 2024'te Devenish, Ocak 2026'da Biomatrix ve Nutribins alındı. Alımlar ana işle ilgili, ama borçla yapıldı: kaynağa göre net borç/FAVÖK 2,07. Şerefiyenin özsermayeye oranı, hisse bazlı ücret ve bilanço dışı yükümlülükler: bakıldı, şirket belgesi açılamadığı için okunamadı.
353810.latest: 14 Ağustos 2026: İkinci çeyrekte gelir 148,1 milyar won, faaliyet kârı 15,1 milyar won, net kâr 10,9 milyar won (geçen yıl 113,8 milyar, 11,0 milyar ve 4,1 milyar won). İlk yarıda faaliyet kârı 28,3 milyar won (geçen yıl 20,1 milyar; +%41). Rakamlar bir veri sitesinden; üçüncü çeyrek sonuçları bu çalıştırmada bulunamadı.

en.one: Maker of feed additives and piglet feed; it bought US-based Devenish with debt in 2024. It did not pass the moat test: margin is around 10% and there is no market share evidence.
en.business: Easy Bio makes animal feed additives and piglet feed. About 74.8% of revenue comes from feed additives and 25.2% from compound feed. In March 2024 it bought US-based Devenish Nutrition, which was larger than itself; revenue went from about 165 billion won to 384 billion won in 2024 and the overseas share passed 60%. In 2025 revenue was about 477 billion won and operating profit about 45 billion won (margin 9.4%). In the first half of 2026 revenue was 278.8 billion won and operating profit 28.3 billion won.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. There is an advantage: customers are reluctant to switch specialty feed additives, and additive margins are several times those of ordinary feed (2-3%). But the numbers do not prove a narrow moat. Consolidated operating margin was 10.4% in 2022, 12.5% in 2023, 8.4% in 2024 and 9.4% in 2025: not high, and it fell with the acquisition. No market share figure appears in any document read. In compound feed about 80% of cost is grain; the price is passed on to customers, but this is a commodity business. Part of the high return on equity (latest real reading 34.3%) comes from debt: at the end of 2024 liabilities were about three times equity, and return on invested capital stayed in the 14-17% range. Growth came through acquisitions; Devenish's margin was around 4% before the purchase.
en.mgmt: The main shareholder is Easy Holdings with three related persons: 51.53%. The company was formed by a split from Easy Holdings in 2020; the group's chicken, duck and pig farms are its customers, so there are related-party sales (the amount could not be read). Profit goes to dividends and acquisitions: dividend per share was 75 won in 2022, 100 in 2023 and 200 in 2024; the payout ratio was 21-33%. It bought Devenish in March 2024 and Biomatrix and Nutribins in January 2026. The purchases are related to the main business but were made with debt: net debt/EBITDA is 2.07 according to the source. Goodwill relative to equity, share-based pay and off-balance-sheet obligations: looked for, but could not be read because the company document could not be opened.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: In the second quarter revenue was 148.1 billion won, operating profit 15.1 billion won and net profit 10.9 billion won (a year earlier 113.8 billion, 11.0 billion and 4.1 billion won). First-half operating profit was 28.3 billion won (20.1 billion a year earlier; +41%). Figures are from a data site; third-quarter results could not be found in this run.
risks: Debt is high: on the end-2025 estimate, liabilities are about 2.3 times equity; interest and exchange rates affect profit directly.

Most of the profit now comes from the United States; the inflation adjustment uses Korean inflation, and US herd sizes and tariffs move the results (weakness was seen in the second and third quarters of 2025).
Growth relies on acquisitions; the amount of goodwill could not be read.

Üstünlük sayılabilecek yanlar: Cisco Gold belgesi ve kurulan ağın bakımından gelen, gelirin üçte birini aşan yinelenen iş. en.one: Builds and maintains corporate networks with Cisco equipment. It did not pass the moat test: work is won by bidding and the operating margin is 6%.
en.business: OPASnet builds computer networks for companies and public bodies and then maintains them. Most of the equipment comes from Cisco; the company has been a Cisco Gold partner since 2011. In 2025 revenue was 233.3 billion won, operating profit 14.0 billion won and net profit attributable to owners 12.7 billion won. Network construction revenue was 137.1 billion won (+21.5%) and maintenance revenue 82.8 billion won (+24.9%; 35.6% of revenue). Customers include SK Telecom, Samsung SDS, financial institutions and public bodies.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. The business is installing and selling equipment made by someone else; projects are won by bids and tenders. The numbers show it: in 2025 gross margin was 17.2% and operating margin 6.0% (5.5% in 2024). There are rivals doing the same work (Insung Information, S-Net). What could count as an advantage: the Cisco Gold certification and recurring maintenance work on installed networks, which is more than a third of revenue. These set the company apart from a pure tender business, but pricing power does not show in the margins and there is dependence on a single supplier. Real return on equity averaged 17.5% over five years; that is the result of a service business that runs on little capital rather than of a moat.
en.mgmt: Chief executive Jang Su-hyun owns 25.29%; with related persons 41.30%. Other large holders are Kim Yoon-jung with 7.41% and Park Geon-sang with 7.17%. The company has net cash (net debt/EBITDA of -2.73 in the source). Profit has started to return to owners: dividend per share was 100 won in 2024 and 250 won in 2025. No large investment outside the main business and no share issuance were seen. Share-based pay, goodwill and off-balance-sheet obligations: looked for, but could not be read because the company document could not be opened.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: In the second quarter revenue was 47.3 billion won, operating profit 1.9 billion won and net profit 3.6 billion won (a year earlier 58.2 billion, 5.6 billion and 4.6 billion won). First-half operating profit was 3.3 billion won (6.2 billion a year earlier). According to a data site, third-quarter revenue was 51.0 billion won and operating profit 1.8 billion won (42.8 billion and 3.4 billion won a year earlier). Figures are from data sites; the company's own document could not be opened.
risks: Operating profit is falling in 2026: from 6.2 billion won to 3.3 billion won in the first half, and from 3.4 billion won to 1.8 billion won in the third quarter.
Revenue depends on customers' information technology spending and on a single supplier (Cisco).

214150.business: Classys, kliniklere ameliyatsız cilt sıkılaştırma cihazları satar: odaklı ultrason (Shurink, yurt dışında Ultraformer) ve radyo frekansı (Volnewmer). Cihaz satıldıktan sonra her işlemde tükenen başlıkları da satar. 2025'te gelir 336,8 milyar won, faaliyet kârı 170,6 milyar won, net kâr 131,9 milyar won. 2026'nın ilk çeyreğinde gelirin %48'i cihaz, %47'si sarf malzemesiydi. Gelirin dörtte üçe yakını yurt dışından gelir; şirket Brezilya ve Japonya'da distribütörden kendi satış örgütüne geçti.
214150.moat_text: Hendek dar. Kanıt: brüt kâr marjı 2023'te %78,0, 2024'te %78,7, 2025'te %77,5; faaliyet kâr marjı 2025'te %50,7. Kurulu cihazlar yinelenen başlık satışı getirir. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda %23 ile %32 arasında kaldı. Zayıf yanlar 2026'da görünür oldu: brüt marj üçüncü çeyrekte %73,7'ye indi; Kore'de tıbbi cihaz geliri üç çeyrektir düşüyor (üçüncü çeyrekte cihaz %45, sarf malzemesi %29 geriledi). Basına göre şirket Kore odaklı ultrason pazarındaki payını yaklaşık %55 diye tahmin ediyor; bu rakam şirket belgesinden doğrulanamadı. Çin'de üç yerli ve bir ithal rakip cihaz onay aldı. Kalıcılık belirsiz olduğu için sınıf geniş değil.
214150.mgmt: En büyük ortak Bain Capital: 2022'de %60,84 payı yaklaşık 670 milyar wona aldı, Mayıs 2025 ve Şubat 2026'da blok satış yaptı, payı %45,91'e indi (30.072.418 pay). Faaliyet kârı ile vergi öncesi kâr arasındaki yaklaşık 19 milyar wonluk farkın nedeni okunamadı. 12 Ağustos 2026'da 2026 gelir beklentisi 470-510 milyar wondan 430-460 milyar wona indirildi.
risks: Kâr geriliyor: eylül sonuna kadarki 12 ayda hisse başına kâr yaklaşık 1.697 won (2025'te 2.014). Evrendeki F/K artık bu döneme göre. Üçüncü çeyrekteki yaklaşık 19 milyar wonluk faaliyet dışı kaybın nedeni okunamadı; yinelenirse kazanç daha da düşer.
Kore'de tıbbi cihaz geliri üç çeyrektir düşüyor (üçüncü çeyrekte -%35,9); rekabet artıyor ve ana ürün yenileniyor.
Bain Capital şirketi satmak istiyor ve payları karşılığında borçlu; yeni bir blok satış ya da el değiştirme yönetimi ve temettü politikasını değiştirebilir.
Brezilya ve Japonya'da doğrudan satışa geçiş marjı düşürdü: faaliyet kâr marjı 2025'te %50,7 iken üçüncü çeyrekte %32,5.
Çin onayı gecikiyor (Volnewmer eylülden aralığa kaydı) ve Çin'de radyo frekansı cihazları artık klinik deneme gerektiren sınıfta.

en.one: Sells skin-tightening devices and consumables. The moat is narrow; profit is falling in 2026 and third-quarter net profit fell 81%. The price fall is real, with no share split.
en.business: Classys sells non-surgical skin-tightening devices to clinics: focused ultrasound (Shurink, sold abroad as Ultraformer) and radio frequency (Volnewmer). After a device is sold it also sells the cartridges and tips used up in each treatment. In 2025 revenue was 336.8 billion won, operating profit 170.6 billion won and net profit 131.9 billion won. In the first quarter of 2026, 48% of revenue was devices and 47% consumables. Close to three quarters of revenue comes from abroad; the company has moved from distributors to its own sales organisation in Brazil and Japan.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Evidence: gross margin was 78.0% in 2023, 78.7% in 2024 and 77.5% in 2025; operating margin was 50.7% in 2025. Installed devices bring recurring consumable sales. Real return on equity stayed between 23% and 32% over five years. The weak points became visible in 2026: gross margin fell to 73.7% in the third quarter; medical device revenue in Korea has fallen for three quarters (in the third quarter devices fell 45% and consumables 29%). According to the press the company estimates its share of the Korean focused ultrasound market at about 55%; this figure could not be confirmed in a company document. In China three local rival devices and one imported one have been approved. Because durability is uncertain, the class is not wide.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is Bain Capital: it bought 60.84% in 2022 for about 670 billion won, sold blocks in May 2025 and February 2026, and now holds 45.91% (30,072,418 shares). Bain wants to sell the company; the press reports that it has borrowed against its shares. The chief executive changed in August 2026 (Yoon Jun-oh). Profit distribution: 1,000 won per share for 2025, 65.2 billion won in total, 49.4% of profit. The Brazilian distributor Medsystems was acquired in March 2026; the Brazilian unit carries 62.5 billion won of borrowings. The company missed its 2025 revenue target and cut its 2026 revenue outlook in August. Intangible assets were 146.3 billion won in March 2026 (about 28% of equity); goodwill is not shown separately. According to the source the share count rose 0.4% in 2024 and 1.8% in 2025. Share-based pay (options were granted in July 2026), buyback prices and off-balance-sheet obligations: checked, not in the documents that could be opened.
en.latest: 12 November 2026: In the third quarter revenue was 83.0 billion won (flat on a year earlier), operating profit 27.0 billion won (-28.2%), pre-tax profit 7.7 billion won and net profit attributable to owners 6.3 billion won (-81.0%). The figures are preliminary and not yet reviewed by the auditor. For nine months revenue was 275.7 billion won (+13.3%), operating profit 108.1 billion won (-9.4%) and net profit attributable to owners 68.3 billion won (-23.6%); earnings per share were 1,047 won (1,364 a year earlier). The company gave these reasons: a product generation change in Korea and the cost of moving to direct sales in Brazil and Japan. The reason for the gap of about 19 billion won between operating profit and pre-tax profit could not be read. On 12 August 2026 the 2026 revenue outlook was cut from 470-510 billion won to 430-460 billion won.
risks: Profit is falling: earnings per share for the 12 months to end-September are about 1,697 won (2,014 in 2025). The P/E in the dataset is now on this period. The reason for the non-operating loss of about 19 billion won in the third quarter could not be read; if it recurs, earnings fall further.
Medical device revenue in Korea has fallen for three quarters (-35.9% in the third quarter); competition is rising and the main product is being renewed.
Bain Capital wants to sell the company and has borrowed against its shares; another block sale or a change of control could change management and dividend policy.
The move to direct sales in Brazil and Japan has lowered margins: operating margin was 50.7% in 2025 and 32.5% in the third quarter.
Chinese approval is slipping (Volnewmer moved from September to December) and radio frequency devices in China are now in the class that requires clinical trials.

445180.business: Purit, yarı iletken üretiminde ışığa duyarlı kaplamayı temizleyen tinerin ham maddelerini üretir: PGMEA ve PGME'yi saflaştırır, etil laktat (EL) ve EEP'yi sentezler, kullanılmış çözücüleri geri kazanır. 445180.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu yüzden 3. suru geçemedi. Üstünlük var: yarı iletken sınıfı EL'yi 2021'de Kore'de ilk üreten şirket ve müşteri onayı uzun sürer. Basına göre Samsung'a giden EL'de payı 2026'da yaklaşık %40'a çıktı; bu rakam şirketin kendi belgesinde doğrulanamadı. Marjlar dar bir hendeği kanıtlamıyor. Şirketin sunumuna göre brüt kâr marjı 2022'de %15,9, 2023'te %18,0, 2024'te %20,0; faaliyet kâr marjı %10,4, %10,7 ve %11,4. 2025'te faaliyet kâr marjı yaklaşık %12, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde %12,7. Marj yükseliyor ama düzeyi bir saflaştırma ve fason işleme işininkidir; aracı kuruma göre saflaştırmada marj %10-12, geri kazanımda %5-7. Satışlar bağımsız müşteriyle sınanmış değil: 2022'de satışların %65,9'u ilişkili taraflara yapıldı (ENF Technology 51,8 milyar won, KCNA 37,9 milyar won); ikisi de ana ortak Hankook Alcohol Industrial'ın grubundandır. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı 2021'de %28,2 iken 2024'te %11,3'e indi; son okuma %13,9.
445180.mgmt: Ana ortak Hankook Alcohol Industrial: %48,71; ilişkili yöneticilerle birlikte %50,39 (7 Ekim 2026). Şirket Hankook Alcohol'ün konsolide bağlı ortaklığıdır; aynı grup hem ham madde satar hem de en büyük müşterilerin sahibidir. Bu, küçük ortak açısından izlenecek bir ilişkili taraf yapısıdır; güncel tutarlar okunamadı. Kârın büyük bölümü şirkette kalıyor: hisse başına temettü 2023'te 50, 2024 ve 2025'te 120 won; dağıtım oranı %14-17. Para Yesan'daki yeni fabrikaya gidiyor: arsa için yaklaşık 9,6 milyar won ödendi, donanım için yaklaşık 35 milyar won planlanıyor; ikinci fabrikanın genişlemesi 17,5 milyar won. Yatırım ana işle ilgili. Net nakit var (kaynakta net borç/FAVÖK -1,02). Pay sayısı: Ekim 2023'teki halka arzda 2.887.000 yeni pay çıkarıldı; ödenmiş sermaye 2022 sonunda 6,9 milyar wondan 2023 sonunda 8,4 milyar wona çıktı. Kaynağın beş yıllık sulandırma rakamının büyük bölümü 2021'deki bir pay sayısı değişiminden geliyor; nedeni belgede okunamadı. Yöneticilere 2.000 wondan kullanılan pay opsiyonları var; Ekim 2026'da 50.000 pay çıkarıldı (toplam 17.239.188). Şerefiye: tek şirket tablosu, satın alma görülmedi. Hisse bazlı ücretin tutarı ve bilanço dışı yükümlülükler: bakıldı, yıllık rapor açılamadığı için okunamadı.
445180.latest: 19 Kasım 2026: Basının aktardığı sonuç duyurusuna göre üçüncü çeyrekte faaliyet kârı 6,03 milyar won (geçen yıla göre +%14,9), gelir %28,4 arttı, faaliyet kâr marjı %12,7. Faaliyet kârı önceki çeyreğin (6,5 milyar won) altında kaldı; şirket bunu kurdaki düşüşe ve sanayi ürünlerindeki zayıf talebe bağladı. Çeyreğin net kârı okunamadı. İkinci çeyrekte (13 Ağustos 2026) gelir 44,9 milyar won, faaliyet kârı 6,5 milyar won, net kâr 5,3 milyar wondu; bu rakamlar bir veri sitesinden.

Son kullanıcı iki şirket: Samsung Electronics ve SK hynix. Talep bu fabrikaların doluluk oranına bağlı; bellek döngüsü şu an yükselişte, beş yıl tam bir döngüyü göstermez.

en.one: Purifies and synthesises raw materials for semiconductor thinner. It did not pass the moat test: operating margin of 11-13%, most sales to the parent's group.
en.business: Purit makes the raw materials of the thinner that cleans photoresist in chip making: it purifies PGMEA and PGME, synthesises ethyl lactate (EL) and EEP, and recycles used solvents. Products are sold to thinner makers (ENF Technology, Dongjin Semichem); the end users are Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. In the first nine months of 2025 about 75% of revenue came from semiconductors. In 2025 revenue was 142.5 billion won and operating profit 17.2 billion won; in 2024 revenue was 122.5 billion won and net profit 11.8 billion won. The statements are for a single company; there are no subsidiaries.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass the third wall. There is an advantage: it was the first company in Korea to make semiconductor-grade EL, in 2021, and customer qualification takes a long time. According to the press its share of the EL going to Samsung rose to about 40% in 2026; this figure could not be confirmed in the company's own documents. The margins do not prove a narrow moat. According to the company's presentation the gross margin was 15.9% in 2022, 18.0% in 2023 and 20.0% in 2024; the operating margin was 10.4%, 10.7% and 11.4%. The operating margin was about 12% in 2025 and 12.7% in the third quarter of 2026. The margin is rising, but its level is that of a purification and toll-processing business; a broker puts the margin at 10-12% in purification and 5-7% in recycling. Sales have not been tested with independent customers: in 2022, 65.9% of sales went to related parties (ENF Technology 51.8 billion won, KCNA 37.9 billion won); both belong to the group of the parent, Hankook Alcohol Industrial. Real return on equity fell from 28.2% in 2021 to 11.3% in 2024; the latest reading is 13.9%.
en.mgmt: The parent is Hankook Alcohol Industrial: 48.71%; 50.39% together with related executives (7 October 2026). The company is a consolidated subsidiary of Hankook Alcohol; the same group both sells it raw materials and owns its largest customers. This is a related-party structure for a minority shareholder to watch; current amounts could not be read. Most of the profit stays in the company: the dividend per share was 50 won for 2023 and 120 won for 2024 and 2025; the payout ratio is 14-17%. The money goes to the new plant in Yesan: about 9.6 billion won was paid for land and about 35 billion won is planned for equipment; the expansion of the second plant is 17.5 billion won. The investment is in the core business. There is net cash (net debt/EBITDA of -1.02 in the source). Share count: 2,887,000 new shares were issued in the October 2023 listing; paid-in capital rose from 6.9 billion won at the end of 2022 to 8.4 billion won at the end of 2023. Most of the source's five-year dilution figure comes from a change in the share count in 2021; its cause could not be read in a document. Executives hold stock options exercisable at 2,000 won; 50,000 shares were issued in October 2026 (total 17,239,188). Goodwill: single-company statements, no acquisition seen. The amount of share-based pay and off-balance-sheet liabilities: checked, could not be read because the annual report could not be opened.
en.latest: 19 November 2026: According to the results release as reported by the press, third-quarter operating profit was 6.03 billion won (+14.9% on a year earlier), revenue rose 28.4% and the operating margin was 12.7%. Operating profit was below the previous quarter (6.5 billion won); the company put this down to the fall in the exchange rate and weak demand for industrial products. The quarter's net profit could not be read. In the second quarter (13 August 2026) revenue was 44.9 billion won, operating profit 6.5 billion won and net profit 5.3 billion won; these figures are from a data site.
risks: Most sales go to companies in the parent's group (65.9% in 2022); that prices are set on market terms could not be confirmed from a company document.
There are two end users: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. Demand depends on the utilisation of their plants; the memory cycle is now rising, and five years do not show a full cycle.

The new plant investment (about 35 billion won of equipment, up to 100 billion won in total later) is large relative to equity; 85% of profit stays in the company and the return on that money has not yet been seen.
Capacity in PGMEA and PGME is nearly full; growth depends on a rising share in EL and EEP.

272110.one: Çip üretiminde tükenen silisyum karbür halkalar yapan şirket. Hendek zayıf: pazar payı ve müşteriler açıklanmıyor, marj düşüyor, net kâr geriliyor; 3. suru geçemedi.
272110.business: KnJ, çip üretiminin aşındırma adımında kullanılan ve zamanla tükenen silisyum karbür (CVD-SiC) odak halkalarını üretir. Üretim Asan ve Dangjin'dedir. 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında gelir 108,1 milyar won (+%81,2), faaliyet kârı 23,9 milyar won (+%43,9). Yarı iletken parçaları 80,5 milyar won gelir ve 20,6 milyar won faaliyet kârı getirdi. Kalan gelirin büyük bölümü, 2025 sonunda konsolide edilen esnek devre kartı üreticisi Circuit Flex'ten geliyor (25,8 milyar won; faaliyet kâr marjı yaklaşık %12). Şirket ekran ekipmanı işinden 2024'te çıktı.
272110.moat_text: Hendek zayıf. Üstünlük var: halka, müşterinin üretim hattında onaydan geçmeden satılamaz; tükenen parça olduğu için satış yinelenir. Yarı iletken parçalarında faaliyet kâr marjı ilk dokuz ayda %25,6. Ama kanıt dar hendek için yetmiyor. Şirket pazar payını açıklamıyor; hedefi 2030'da Kore pazarında %20'nin üstü, yani bugün daha küçük bir tedarikçi. Müşteri adları ve payları açılan belgelerde yok; basın, hacmin çoğunun bellek üreticilerine gittiğini yazıyor. Fiyatlama gücü görünmüyor: faaliyet kâr marjı 2024'te %29 iken 2026'nın ilk yarısında %20,2'ye indi; gelir %81 büyürken faaliyet kârı %44 büyüdü. Kaynağa göre yatırılan sermayenin getirisi beş yılda %7 ile %15 arasında; serbest nakit akışı son iki dönemde eksi. Ölçek büyük sermaye istiyor ve üstünlük bir iki büyük alıcının kararına bağlı.
272110.mgmt: En büyük ortak genel müdür Shim Ho-seop: %14,11; yakınlarıyla birlikte %24,3 (2025 sonu). Focus One Investment Purpose Company %10,4 bildirdi (Şubat 2026). Kâr ana işin dışına da gidiyor: şirket otomotiv esnek devre kartı üreticisi Circuit Flex'i bir yatırım şirketi üzerinden aldı ve 2025 sonunda konsolide etti; bağlı kuruluşları arasında girişim sermayesi fonları ve bir girişim sermayesi şirketi var. Ocak 2026'da 20 milyar wonluk faizsiz, yedi yıl vadeli tahvil ihraç edildi: paya çevrilirse 931.315 yeni pay doğar (yaklaşık %11,6); dönüştürme fiyatı 21.475 won, fiyat düşerse 15.032 wona kadar iner. Mayıs 2026'da Pyeongtaek'te 43,6 milyar wona arsa alındı (2025 sonu toplam aktifin %18,91'i). Eylül 2026'da 3 milyar wonluk geri alım kararı alındı (126.315 pay, iptal edilecek); alım fiyatı açılan belgelerde yok. Kaynakta temettü yok. Eylül 2025 sonunda net borç 55,6 milyar won idi. Hisse bazlı ücret, şerefiye (Circuit Flex alımından doğan) ve bilanço dışı yükümlülükler: bakıldı, açılan belgelerde yok; şirketin DART'taki raporu açılamadı.
272110.latest: 12 Kasım 2026: Şirket üçüncü çeyrek raporunu açıkladı. Çeyrekte gelir 39,1 milyar won (+%82,9), faaliyet kârı 10,0 milyar won (+%75,3), net kâr 5,6 milyar won (-%24,7). Dokuz ayda gelir 108,1 milyar won (+%81,2), faaliyet kârı 23,9 milyar won (+%43,9), net kâr 12,3 milyar won (-%21,1). Basına göre şirket net kârdaki düşüşü vergi giderinin artmasına bağlıyor; ilk yarıda ayrıca tahvilin nakit dışı değerleme zararı ve 1 Ağustos 2026'da devredilen yurt dışı bağlı şirketin zararı vardı. Asan'daki yeni tesis temmuzda devreye girdi; çeyreklik kapasite yaklaşık 25 milyar wondan 35 milyar wona çıktı. Rakamlar DART raporunu aktaran basından; raporun kendisi açılamadı.
risks: Son 12 ayın kârı işin olağan kazancını olduğundan yüksek gösteriyor: 2025'te net kâr (25,6 milyar won) faaliyet kârını (22,2 milyar won) aştı; farkın kaynağı (faaliyet dışı gelir ve düşük vergi) şirket belgesinden okunamadı. 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında net kâr %21,1 geriledi.
Kazanç çip yatırım döngüsüne bağlı: talep bellek üreticilerinin kapasite kullanımıyla yükselir ve düşer. Beş yıl tam bir döngüyü göstermez; bugün döngünün güçlü yanındayız.
Müşteriler az sayıda büyük çip üreticisi; adları ve payları açıklanmıyor. Bir müşterinin başka tedarikçiye dönmesi geliri hemen düşürür.
Şirket borçla ve tahville büyüyor: net borç/FAVÖK kaynakta 2,2; 43,6 milyar wonluk arsa ve yeni tesisler sırada. Tahvil paya çevrilirse pay sayısı yaklaşık %11,6 artar.
Sermayenin bir bölümü ana işle ilgisi az alanlara gidiyor: esnek devre kartı (Circuit Flex) ve girişim sermayesi fonları.

en.one: Makes silicon carbide rings that wear out in chip production. The moat is weak: market share and customers are not disclosed, margins are falling and net profit is down; it did not pass the third wall.
en.business: KnJ makes silicon carbide (CVD-SiC) focus rings, which are used in the etching step of chip production and wear out over time. Production is in Asan and Dangjin. In the first nine months of 2026 revenue was 108.1 billion won (+81.2%) and operating profit 23.9 billion won (+43.9%). Semiconductor parts brought 80.5 billion won of revenue and 20.6 billion won of operating profit. Most of the rest comes from Circuit Flex, a flexible circuit board maker consolidated at the end of 2025 (25.8 billion won; operating margin about 12%). The company left the display equipment business in 2024.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. There is an advantage: a ring cannot be sold until it is qualified on the customer's production line, and because it is a consumable the sale repeats. Operating margin in semiconductor parts was 25.6% in the first nine months. But the evidence falls short of a narrow moat. The company does not disclose its market share; its target is more than 20% of the Korean market by 2030, so today it is a smaller supplier. Customer names and shares are not in the documents that could be opened; the press says most volume goes to memory makers. Pricing power does not show: operating margin was 29% in 2024 and fell to 20.2% in the first half of 2026; revenue grew 81% while operating profit grew 44%. According to the source, return on invested capital was between 7% and 15% over five years; free cash flow was negative in the last two periods. Scale needs heavy capital and the advantage depends on the decisions of one or two large buyers.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is chief executive Shim Ho-seop: 14.11%; 24.3% with related parties (end of 2025). Focus One Investment Purpose Company reported 10.4% (February 2026). Profit also goes outside the core business: the company bought automotive flexible circuit board maker Circuit Flex through an investment vehicle and consolidated it at the end of 2025; its subsidiaries include venture capital funds and a venture capital firm. In January 2026 it issued a 20 billion won zero-coupon seven-year convertible bond: conversion would create 931,315 new shares (about 11.6%); the conversion price is 21,475 won and can reset down to 15,032 won if the share price falls. In May 2026 it bought land in Pyeongtaek for 43.6 billion won (18.91% of total assets at the end of 2025). In September 2026 it decided on a 3 billion won buyback (126,315 shares, to be cancelled); the purchase price is not in the documents that could be opened. The source shows no dividend. Net debt was 55.6 billion won at the end of September 2025. Share-based pay, goodwill (from the Circuit Flex acquisition) and off-balance-sheet obligations: checked, not in the documents that could be opened; the company's report on DART could not be opened.
en.latest: 12 November 2026: The company filed its third-quarter report. In the quarter revenue was 39.1 billion won (+82.9%), operating profit 10.0 billion won (+75.3%) and net profit 5.6 billion won (-24.7%). For nine months revenue was 108.1 billion won (+81.2%), operating profit 23.9 billion won (+43.9%) and net profit 12.3 billion won (-21.1%). According to the press the company attributes the fall in net profit to higher tax expense; in the first half there were also a non-cash valuation loss on the convertible bond and the loss of a foreign subsidiary transferred on 1 August 2026. The new Asan plant started in July; quarterly capacity rose from about 25 billion won to 35 billion won. The figures are from press reports of the DART filing; the filing itself could not be opened.
risks: Last-12-month profit overstates the normal earnings of the business: in 2025 net profit (25.6 billion won) exceeded operating profit (22.2 billion won); the source of the gap (non-operating income and low tax) could not be read in a company document. In the first nine months of 2026 net profit fell 21.1%.
Earnings depend on the chip investment cycle: demand rises and falls with memory makers' capacity utilisation. Five years do not show a full cycle; today we are on the strong side of the cycle.
Customers are a small number of large chipmakers; their names and shares are not disclosed. One customer switching to another supplier would lower revenue at once.

The company is growing with debt and a convertible bond: net debt/EBITDA is 2.2 in the source; the 43.6 billion won site and new plants are ahead. If the bond converts, the share count rises by about 11.6%.
Part of the capital goes to areas with little link to the core business: flexible circuit boards (Circuit Flex) and venture capital funds.
